coverage: Both full English editions, all twenty-four books: named people, gods, personified powers, named animals and named peoples. Places, rivers, mountains, islands, ships, stars and adjectival forms of place names are excluded.

entities.name: Odysseus
entities.body: King of Ithaca, husband of Penelope and father of Telemachus. He sacked Troy and has been twenty years getting home. Butler’s original calls him by his Roman name, Ulysses.

entities.name: Telemachus
entities.body: Odysseus’s son, a young man who has grown up without ever meeting his father.

snapshots.body: Odysseus’s son. He has now met his father, who revealed himself to him at the swineherd’s hut.

entities.name: Penelope
entities.body: Odysseus’s wife, holding his household together against the suitors who want her to remarry.

entities.name: Laertes
entities.body: Odysseus’s father, the old king of Ithaca, who has withdrawn to his farm in the country.

entities.name: Anticlea
entities.body: Odysseus’s mother, daughter of Autolycus.

entities.name: Euryclea
entities.body: The old nurse of Odysseus’s house, bought by Laertes; she nursed Odysseus and then Telemachus. The modern edition spells her name both Euryclea and Eurycleia.

entities.name: Eumaeus
entities.body: Odysseus’s swineherd, who keeps the pig farm in the hills and is loyal to the absent master.

snapshots.body: Odysseus’s swineherd, loyal to the absent master. He was born a king’s son on the island of Syra, the child of Ctesius son of Ormenus.

entities.name: Philoetius
entities.body: Odysseus’s stockman, in charge of the cattle on the mainland.

entities.name: Melanthius
entities.body: Odysseus’s goatherd, son of Dolius, who has taken the suitors’ side.

entities.name: Eurynome
entities.body: Penelope’s head waiting woman and housekeeper.

entities.name: Dolius
entities.body: The old gardener given to Penelope by her father when she married; father of Melanthius and Melantho.

entities.name: Melantho
entities.body: A maid of the house, daughter of Dolius, brought up by Penelope; she sides with the suitors.

entities.name: Medon
entities.body: A servant and herald of Odysseus’s house who waits on the suitors at table.

entities.name: Phemius
entities.body: The bard of Ithaca, son of Terpes, forced to sing for the suitors.

entities.name: The maid who keeps the bedroom door
entities.body: Penelope’s maidservant, daughter of Actor, the only servant who knows the secret of the marriage bed.

entities.name: Argos
entities.body: Odysseus’s hunting dog, bred by him before he left for Troy and now old and neglected.

entities.name: Ctimene
entities.body: Odysseus’s younger sister, brought up alongside Eumaeus and married away to Same.

entities.name: Antinous
entities.body: Son of Eupeithes and the most aggressive of the suitors courting Penelope.

entities.name: Eurymachus
entities.body: Son of Polybus and, with Antinous, a leader among the suitors.

entities.name: Amphinomus
entities.body: A suitor from Dulichium, son of Nisus; the most decent-spoken of them, and Penelope’s favourite among them.

entities.name: Agelaus
entities.body: A suitor, son of Damastor.

entities.name: Ctesippus
entities.body: A suitor from Same, a coarse-mannered rich man’s son.

entities.name: Leiodes
entities.body: A suitor, son of Oenops, who acts as sacrificial priest to the others.

entities.name: Eurynomus
entities.body: A suitor, one of the three surviving sons of the old Ithacan Aegyptius.

entities.name: Amphimedon
entities.body: A suitor of Ithaca, son of Melaneus, who once hosted Agamemnon.

entities.name: Demoptolemus
entities.body: A suitor who fights in the front rank at the end.

entities.name: Pisander
entities.body: A suitor, son of Polyctor.

entities.name: Polybus
entities.body: A suitor, son of Polyctor.

entities.name: Polybus
entities.body: Father of the suitor Eurymachus.

entities.name: Eurydamas
entities.body: A suitor.

entities.name: Leocritus
entities.body: A suitor, son of Evenor, who breaks up the Ithacan assembly. Butler’s original spells him Leiocritus at his first appearance.

entities.name: Euryades
entities.body: A suitor killed in the hall.

entities.name: Elatus
entities.body: A suitor killed in the hall.

entities.name: Mulius
entities.body: A servant from Dulichium who waits on Amphinomus.

entities.name: Autonoe
entities.body: One of Penelope’s waiting women.

entities.name: Hippodamia
entities.body: One of Penelope’s waiting women.

entities.name: Irus
entities.body: The town beggar of Ithaca, a big idle man whose real name is Arnaeus; the young men call him Irus because he runs their errands.

snapshots.body: The town beggar of Ithaca, really named Arnaeus, who challenged the stranger at the door and was beaten.

entities.name: Mentor
entities.body: An old friend of Odysseus, left in charge of the household when he sailed for Troy. Athena repeatedly takes his shape and voice.

entities.name: Mentes
entities.body: Chief of the Taphians and an old guest-friend of Odysseus’s house, son of Anchialus; Athena comes to Ithaca in his shape.

entities.name: Halitherses
entities.body: The best reader of omens in Ithaca, son of Mastor, and an old friend of Odysseus’s house.

entities.name: Aegyptius
entities.body: A very old Ithacan who speaks first at the assembly; father of Antiphus, Eurynomus and two sons who work his land.

entities.name: Antiphus
entities.body: Son of the old Ithacan Aegyptius; he sailed with Odysseus and was killed by the Cyclops.

entities.name: Antiphus
entities.body: An elder of Ithaca, one of the old friends of Odysseus’s house with whom Telemachus sits in the assembly.

entities.name: Eupeithes
entities.body: Father of Antinous; Odysseus once saved him from an Ithacan mob.

entities.name: Noemon
entities.body: An Ithacan, son of Phronius, who lends Telemachus a ship.

entities.name: Phronius
entities.body: Father of Noemon.

entities.name: Piraeus
entities.body: Telemachus’s friend, son of Clytius, who keeps his guest and his gifts while the house is unsafe.

entities.name: Clytius
entities.body: Father of Piraeus.

entities.name: Theoclymenus
entities.body: A seer of the house of Melampus, in exile from Argos for killing a man; Telemachus brings him home to Ithaca.

snapshots.body: The seer Telemachus brought home from Pylos, of the house of Melampus; he reads the darkness that falls over the suitors at their meal.

entities.name: Pisenor
entities.body: The herald of the Ithacan assembly, who brings Telemachus his staff.

entities.name: Evenor
entities.body: Father of the suitor Leocritus.

entities.name: Damastor
entities.body: Father of the suitor Agelaus.

entities.name: Polyctor
entities.body: Father of the suitors Pisander and Polybus.

entities.name: Oenops
entities.body: Father of the suitor Leiodes.

entities.name: Melaneus
entities.body: An Ithacan, father of the suitor Amphimedon.

entities.name: Nisus
entities.body: A rich and brave man of Dulichium, son of Aretias and father of Amphinomus.

entities.name: Aretias
entities.body: A king, father of Nisus and grandfather of Amphinomus.

entities.name: Polytherses
entities.body: Father of the suitor Ctesippus.

entities.name: Mastor
entities.body: Father of the seer Halitherses.

entities.name: Terpes
entities.body: Father of the bard Phemius.

entities.name: Ops
entities.body: Father of the nurse Euryclea, son of Pisenor.

entities.name: Pisenor
entities.body: Father of Ops and grandfather of the nurse Euryclea.

entities.name: Icarius
entities.body: Penelope’s father.

entities.name: Iphthime
entities.body: Penelope’s sister, daughter of Icarius, married to Eumelus of Pherae; Athena sends a phantom in her likeness.

entities.name: Eumelus
entities.body: Iphthime’s husband, who lives at Pherae.

entities.name: Arceisius
entities.body: Odysseus’s grandfather, father of Laertes.

entities.name: Autolycus
entities.body: Odysseus’s maternal grandfather, famous as the most accomplished thief and perjurer alive; he named the boy and gave him the boar-hunt scar.

entities.name: Amphithea
entities.body: Odysseus’s grandmother, wife of Autolycus.

entities.name: Icmalius
entities.body: The craftsman who made Penelope’s inlaid chair.

entities.name: Mesaulius
entities.body: A servant Eumaeus bought for himself, who waits at his table.

entities.name: Ithacus
entities.body: One of the three men said to have built the town fountain of Ithaca.

entities.name: Neritus
entities.body: One of the three men said to have built the town fountain of Ithaca.

entities.name: The Sicel woman
entities.body: The old servant who looks after Laertes on his country farm. The modern edition calls her Sicilian.

entities.name: Athena
entities.body: Daughter of Zeus, goddess of war and cunning, and Odysseus’s protector throughout. Butler’s original calls her Minerva.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: King of the gods and father of Athena. Butler’s original calls him Jove.

entities.name: Poseidon
entities.body: God of the sea and the earthquake, and the one god set against Odysseus, because Odysseus blinded his son Polyphemus. Butler’s original calls him Neptune.

entities.name: Hermes
entities.body: The messenger god, guide of travellers and of the dead. Butler’s original calls him Mercury.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: God of archery, prophecy and sudden death.

entities.name: Artemis
entities.body: Goddess of the hunt and Apollo’s sister. Butler’s original calls her Diana.

entities.name: Aphrodite
entities.body: Goddess of love and beauty. Butler’s original calls her Venus.

entities.name: Ares
entities.body: God of war. Butler’s original calls him Mars.

entities.name: Hephaestus
entities.body: The smith of the gods, lame and famously skilful, husband of Aphrodite. Butler’s original calls him Vulcan.

entities.name: Hera
entities.body: Zeus’s wife, queen of the gods. Butler’s original calls her Juno.

entities.name: Demeter
entities.body: Goddess of the harvest. Butler’s original calls her Ceres.

entities.name: Persephone
entities.body: Queen of the dead, who rules in Hades. Butler’s original calls her Proserpine.

entities.name: Hades
entities.body: God of the underworld; the name also stands for his house, where the dead go.

entities.name: Helios
entities.body: The sun god, whose cattle graze on Thrinacia. Butler’s original calls him Hyperion.

entities.name: Cronus
entities.body: Zeus’s father. Butler’s original calls him Saturn.

entities.name: Leto
entities.body: Mother of Apollo and Artemis by Zeus.

entities.name: Dawn
entities.body: The goddess of daybreak, who rises each morning from beside Tithonus. Butler’s original also names her Aurora.

entities.name: Oceanus
entities.body: The great river encircling the earth, spoken of as a god and as the father of nymphs.

entities.name: Amphitrite
entities.body: Sea goddess; the waves are called hers.

entities.name: Proteus
entities.body: The old man of the sea, a shape-shifting immortal who tells the truth only under compulsion.

entities.name: Idothea
entities.body: Daughter of Proteus, who takes pity on Menelaus in Egypt and teaches him how to trap her father.

entities.name: Ino
entities.body: A mortal woman, daughter of Cadmus, since raised to godhood as Leucothea; she gives Odysseus her veil in the storm.

entities.name: Calypso
entities.body: The goddess on Ogygia who kept Odysseus seven years and wanted to marry him.

entities.name: Circe
entities.body: The goddess and enchantress of Aeaea, daughter of the sun and sister of Aeetes.

entities.name: Themis
entities.body: Goddess invoked as the beginning and end of councils.

entities.name: Hebe
entities.body: Daughter of Zeus and Hera, married to Heracles among the gods.

entities.name: Ilithuia
entities.body: Goddess of childbirth, who has a cave at Amnisus in Crete.

entities.name: Paeeon
entities.body: The healer of the gods; the Egyptian physicians are called his race.

entities.name: Bacchus
entities.body: God of wine, who gave the golden urn that holds Achilles’ bones and who denounced Ariadne.

entities.name: Atlas
entities.body: Calypso’s father, who knows the depths of the sea and holds the pillars of heaven apart.

entities.name: Thoosa
entities.body: A sea nymph, daughter of Phorcys and mother of Polyphemus by Poseidon.

entities.name: Phorcys
entities.body: A sea god, father of Thoosa; a harbour of Ithaca bears his name.

entities.name: Crataiis
entities.body: Scylla’s mother, whom Odysseus is told to call on as he passes.

entities.name: Halosydne
entities.body: A sea goddess; the seals are called her flock.

entities.name: Perse
entities.body: Daughter of Oceanus and mother, by the sun, of Circe and Aeetes.

entities.name: Neaera
entities.body: A nymph, mother by Helios of Phaethusa and Lampetie.

entities.name: Phaethusa
entities.body: A goddess, daughter of Helios, who herds the sun’s cattle on Thrinacia with her sister.

entities.name: Lampetie
entities.body: A goddess, daughter of Helios, who herds the sun’s cattle on Thrinacia and reports their slaughter to her father.

entities.name: Maia
entities.body: Hermes’s mother.

entities.name: Thetis
entities.body: A sea goddess, Achilles’ mother, who offered his armour as a prize.

entities.name: The Furies
entities.body: The avenging spirits called down by a wronged parent. Butler’s original names them the Erinyes.

entities.name: The Graces
entities.body: The goddesses who bathe and anoint Aphrodite.

entities.name: The Naiads
entities.body: The water nymphs of the cave above the harbour of Phorcys in Ithaca.

entities.name: Gaia
entities.body: The earth, named as the mother of Tityus.

entities.name: Nestor
entities.body: The old king of Pylos, knight of Gerene, who came home safely from Troy and still gives the best counsel of any Greek.

entities.name: Pisistratus
entities.body: Nestor’s youngest son, who travels with Telemachus to Sparta.

entities.name: Thrasymedes
entities.body: A son of Nestor.

entities.name: Perseus
entities.body: A son of Nestor.

entities.name: Echephron
entities.body: A son of Nestor.

entities.name: Stratius
entities.body: A son of Nestor.

entities.name: Aretus
entities.body: A son of Nestor.

entities.name: Eurydice
entities.body: Nestor’s wife, eldest daughter of Clymenus.

entities.name: Clymenus
entities.body: Father of Nestor’s wife Eurydice.

entities.name: Polycaste
entities.body: Nestor’s youngest daughter, who bathes Telemachus at Pylos.

entities.name: Neleus
entities.body: Nestor’s father, the old king of Pylos, son of Poseidon and Tyro.

entities.name: Laerceus
entities.body: The goldsmith at Pylos who gilds the heifer’s horns for Nestor’s sacrifice.

entities.name: Menelaus
entities.body: King of Sparta, Agamemnon’s brother and Helen’s husband; he came home last of all the Greeks.

entities.name: Helen
entities.body: Menelaus’s wife, daughter of Zeus, whose going to Troy began the war.

entities.name: Megapenthes
entities.body: Menelaus’s son by a slave woman, married on the day Telemachus arrives.

entities.name: Hermione
entities.body: Menelaus and Helen’s only daughter, promised in marriage to Achilles’ son.

entities.name: Eteoneus
entities.body: Menelaus’s servant, son of Boethous, who keeps his door.

entities.name: Boethous
entities.body: Father of Menelaus’s servant Eteoneus.

entities.name: Asphalion
entities.body: A servant of Menelaus who pours water over the guests’ hands.

entities.name: Adraste
entities.body: One of Helen’s maids at Sparta.

entities.name: Alcippe
entities.body: One of Helen’s maids at Sparta.

entities.name: Phylo
entities.body: One of Helen’s maids at Sparta, who fetches her work-box.

entities.name: Alcandra
entities.body: An Egyptian woman of Thebes, wife of Polybus, who gave Helen the silver work-box.

entities.name: Polybus
entities.body: A rich man of Egyptian Thebes who gave Menelaus two silver baths.

entities.name: Polybus
entities.body: The Phaeacian craftsman who made the red ball Laodamas and Halios dance with.

entities.name: Polydamna
entities.body: An Egyptian woman, wife of Thon, who gave Helen the drug that quiets all pain.

entities.name: Thon
entities.body: An Egyptian, husband of Polydamna.

entities.name: Phaedimus
entities.body: King of the Sidonians, who gave Menelaus the silver mixing bowl.

entities.name: Diocles
entities.body: The host at Pherae on the road between Pylos and Sparta, son of Ortilochus.

entities.name: Ortilochus
entities.body: Father of Diocles and grandson of the river Alpheus; his house at Messene is where Odysseus met Iphitus.

entities.name: Alector
entities.body: A Spartan, father of the bride Megapenthes marries.

entities.name: Phrontis
entities.body: The steersman of Menelaus’s ship, the best helmsman alive, killed by Apollo off Sunium.

entities.name: Alcinous
entities.body: King of the Phaeacians on Scheria, son of Nausithous and husband of Arete.

entities.name: Arete
entities.body: Queen of the Phaeacians, Alcinous’s wife and niece, honoured by her people beyond any other woman.

entities.name: Nausicaa
entities.body: Alcinous and Arete’s daughter, who finds Odysseus on the shore.

entities.name: Demodocus
entities.body: The blind bard of the Phaeacian court, whom the Muse loves.

entities.name: Laodamas
entities.body: Alcinous’s son and his favourite, the best looking of the young Phaeacians.

entities.name: Halios
entities.body: A son of Alcinous, who dances with Laodamas. Both editions spell his name Halios once and Halius once.

entities.name: Clytoneus
entities.body: A son of Alcinous who competes in the games.

entities.name: Euryalus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian, son of Naubolus, who taunts Odysseus into the discus throw and then makes amends.

entities.name: Echeneus
entities.body: The oldest of the Phaeacian elders and their best speaker.

entities.name: Pontonous
entities.body: Alcinous’s herald, who mixes and serves the wine.

entities.name: Nausithous
entities.body: The Phaeacians’ former king, son of Poseidon, who moved them from Hypereia to Scheria; father of Alcinous.

entities.name: Rhexenor
entities.body: Nausithous’s elder son, killed young by Apollo; Arete’s father.

entities.name: Periboea
entities.body: Nausithous’s mother, youngest daughter of Eurymedon king of the giants.

entities.name: Eurymedon
entities.body: A king of the giants, whose people and himself were destroyed; Periboea’s father.

entities.name: Eurymedusa
entities.body: The old servant from Apeira, given to Alcinous as a prize, who nursed Nausicaa. The modern edition calls her Eurynome — the name it also gives Penelope’s housekeeper.

entities.name: The sea captain’s daughter
entities.body: Nausicaa’s close friend, daughter of the famous sea captain Dymas; Athena takes her shape.

entities.name: Dymas
entities.body: A famous Phaeacian sea captain.

entities.name: Naubolus
entities.body: Father of the Phaeacian Euryalus.

entities.name: Polyneus
entities.body: A Phaeacian, father of Amphialus and son of Tecton.

entities.name: Tecton
entities.body: A Phaeacian, grandfather of Amphialus.

entities.name: Acroneos
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Ocyalus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Elatreus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Nauteus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Prymneus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Anchialus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Eretmeus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Ponteus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Proreus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Thoon
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Anabesineus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Amphialus
entities.body: A young Phaeacian who competes in the games held for Odysseus.

entities.name: Polyphemus
entities.body: The Cyclops whose cave Odysseus enters, son of Poseidon and the nymph Thoosa.

entities.name: Telemus
entities.body: A seer among the Cyclopes, son of Eurymus, who once prophesied to Polyphemus.

entities.name: Eurymus
entities.body: Father of the Cyclops seer Telemus.

entities.name: Noman
entities.body: The name Odysseus gives the Cyclops when asked. The modern edition renders it Nobody.

entities.name: Aeolus
entities.body: Son of Hippotas and keeper of the winds on his floating island; he gives Odysseus the bag of storms.

entities.name: Hippotas
entities.body: Father of Aeolus the wind king.

entities.name: Antiphates
entities.body: King of the Laestrygonians, who begins the destruction of Odysseus’s fleet.

entities.name: Eurylochus
entities.body: Odysseus’s second in command and kinsman by marriage; he argues against his captain twice.

entities.name: Polites
entities.body: The companion Odysseus valued most of all, who speaks first at Circe’s door.

entities.name: Perimedes
entities.body: One of Odysseus’s crew, who helps at the trench of the dead and at the Sirens.

entities.name: Elpenor
entities.body: The youngest of Odysseus’s crew, neither brave nor clever, who falls from Circe’s roof and is the first ghost to meet him.

entities.name: Teiresias
entities.body: The blind Theban prophet, the one dead man whose understanding Persephone left whole; Odysseus goes to Hades to consult him. The modern edition also spells the name Tiresias.

entities.name: Scylla
entities.body: The six-headed monster in the cliff above the strait, daughter of Crataiis.

entities.name: Charybdis
entities.body: The whirlpool under the fig tree opposite Scylla, which sucks the water down three times a day.

entities.name: The Sirens
entities.body: The singers on their meadow who enchant every man who hears them.

entities.name: The Muse
entities.body: The goddess of song, invoked in the first line and named as the source of Demodocus’s gift.

entities.name: Maron
entities.body: Priest of Apollo at Ismarus, son of Euanthes, who gave Odysseus the strong wine out of gratitude.

entities.name: Euanthes
entities.body: Father of Maron, priest of Apollo at Ismarus.

entities.name: Aeetes
entities.body: A magician, Circe’s brother, and child like her of the sun and Perse.

entities.name: Jason
entities.body: The hero for whose sake Hera steered the Argo safely past the wandering rocks.

entities.name: Lamus
entities.body: The founder whose rocky stronghold is the Laestrygonian city.

entities.name: Agamemnon
entities.body: King of Mycenae and leader of the Greeks at Troy, Menelaus’s brother; he came home to an ambush.

entities.name: Clytemnestra
entities.body: Agamemnon’s wife, daughter of Tyndareus, who took Aegisthus while her husband was at Troy.

entities.name: Aegisthus
entities.body: The man who seduced Clytemnestra and killed Agamemnon, and was killed in turn by Orestes.

entities.name: Orestes
entities.body: Agamemnon’s son, who avenged his father; the example held up to Telemachus.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: Son of Peleus and the greatest of the Greek fighters at Troy.

entities.name: Peleus
entities.body: Achilles’ father, still ruling among the Myrmidons.

entities.name: Aeacus
entities.body: Peleus’s father; Achilles is called his descendant.

entities.name: Patroclus
entities.body: Achilles’ closest companion, killed at Troy.

entities.name: Antilochus
entities.body: Nestor’s son, singularly fast on his feet, killed at Troy.

entities.name: Ajax
entities.body: Son of Telamon and the finest of the Greeks after Achilles; he lost the contest for Achilles’ armour and will not speak to Odysseus even in death.

entities.name: Ajax
entities.body: The Greek leader wrecked on the rocks of Gyrae on the voyage home.

entities.name: Telamon
entities.body: Father of the greater Ajax.

entities.name: Neoptolemus
entities.body: Achilles’ son, whom Odysseus fetched from Scyros; he came home from Troy unharmed.

entities.name: Idomeneus
entities.body: King of Crete, who lost no men at sea coming home from Troy.

entities.name: Philoctetes
entities.body: Son of Poias, an archer who came home safely from Troy.

entities.name: Poias
entities.body: Father of Philoctetes.

entities.name: Diomedes
entities.body: Son of Tydeus, who stationed his ships at Argos on the way home. Butler’s original spells him Diomed.

entities.name: Tydeus
entities.body: Father of Diomedes.

entities.name: Priam
entities.body: King of Troy.

entities.name: Cassandra
entities.body: Priam’s daughter, killed beside Agamemnon by Clytemnestra.

entities.name: Deiphobus
entities.body: A Trojan who was with Helen when she called to the men inside the wooden horse.

entities.name: Anticlus
entities.body: A Greek inside the wooden horse who began to answer Helen’s voice until Odysseus stopped his mouth.

entities.name: Epeus
entities.body: The man who built the wooden horse with Athena’s help.

entities.name: Eurypylus
entities.body: Son of Telephus and the handsomest man Odysseus ever saw except Memnon; killed by Neoptolemus at Troy.

entities.name: Telephus
entities.body: Father of Eurypylus.

entities.name: Memnon
entities.body: A hero named as the handsomest man at Troy.

entities.name: Eurybates
entities.body: Odysseus’s herald at Troy, round-shouldered, dark and curly-haired; his master valued him above the rest.

entities.name: Atreus
entities.body: Father of Agamemnon and Menelaus.

entities.name: Thyestes
entities.body: Atreus’s brother, who used to live on the headland where Aegisthus later settled.

entities.name: Philomeleides
entities.body: The wrestler of Lesbos whom Odysseus threw before the war.

entities.name: Ilus
entities.body: Son of Mermerus, of Ephyra, who feared the gods and would not sell Odysseus arrow poison.

entities.name: Mermerus
entities.body: Father of Ilus of Ephyra.

entities.name: Tyro
entities.body: Daughter of Salmoneus and wife of Cretheus, who bore Pelias and Neleus to Poseidon in the likeness of the river Enipeus.

entities.name: Salmoneus
entities.body: Tyro’s father.

entities.name: Cretheus
entities.body: Son of Aeolus and husband of Tyro.

entities.name: Enipeus
entities.body: A river spoken of as a person, the most beautiful in the world, whose form Poseidon took to deceive Tyro.

entities.name: Pelias
entities.body: Tyro’s son by Poseidon, a great breeder of sheep at Iolcus.

entities.name: Aeson
entities.body: A son of Tyro and Cretheus.

entities.name: Pheres
entities.body: A son of Tyro and Cretheus.

entities.name: Amythaon
entities.body: A son of Tyro and Cretheus, a mighty warrior and charioteer.

entities.name: Antiope
entities.body: Daughter of Asopus, mother by Zeus of Amphion and Zethus.

entities.name: Asopus
entities.body: Antiope’s father.

entities.name: Amphion
entities.body: Son of Zeus and Antiope, who with his brother Zethus founded Thebes and walled it.

entities.name: Zethus
entities.body: Son of Zeus and Antiope, who founded Thebes with Amphion; father of the boy Itylus.

entities.name: Itylus
entities.body: Zethus’s son, killed by mishap by his own mother, who became the nightingale.

entities.name: Pandareus
entities.body: Father of the nightingale of the spring song, and of the daughters the storm winds carried off.

entities.name: Alcmena
entities.body: Wife of Amphitryon and mother of Heracles by Zeus.

entities.name: Amphitryon
entities.body: Alcmena’s husband.

entities.name: Megara
entities.body: Daughter of King Creon, married to Heracles.

entities.name: Creon
entities.body: A great king, father of Megara.

entities.name: Epicaste
entities.body: Mother of Oedipus, who married her own son without knowing it.

entities.name: Oedipodes
entities.body: King of Thebes, who killed his father and married his own mother unknowing. The modern edition calls him Oedipus.

entities.name: Chloris
entities.body: Neleus’s wife and queen in Pylos, youngest daughter of Amphion of Orchomenus; mother of Nestor.

entities.name: Amphion
entities.body: King of Minyan Orchomenus, son of Iasus and father of Chloris.

entities.name: Iasus
entities.body: Father of Amphion king of Orchomenus.

entities.name: Chromius
entities.body: A son of Neleus and Chloris, Nestor’s brother.

entities.name: Periclymenus
entities.body: A son of Neleus and Chloris, Nestor’s brother.

entities.name: Pero
entities.body: Neleus’s daughter, wooed by the whole country and won only through the cattle of Iphicles.

entities.name: Iphicles
entities.body: The owner of the cattle of Phylace that had to be raided to win Pero.

entities.name: Leda
entities.body: Tyndareus’s wife, mother of Castor and Pollux.

entities.name: Tyndarus
entities.body: Leda’s husband and the father of Castor and Pollux. The modern edition spells him Tyndareus.

entities.name: Castor
entities.body: Son of Leda and Tyndareus, a breaker of horses; he and Pollux live and die on alternate days.

entities.name: Pollux
entities.body: Son of Leda and Tyndareus, a mighty boxer.

entities.name: Iphimedeia
entities.body: Wife of Aloeus, who bore Otus and Ephialtes to Poseidon.

entities.name: Aloeus
entities.body: Iphimedeia’s husband.

entities.name: Otus
entities.body: A giant son of Iphimedeia, who with his brother threatened to pile the mountains and storm heaven.

entities.name: Ephialtes
entities.body: A giant son of Iphimedeia, who with his brother threatened to pile the mountains and storm heaven.

entities.name: Phaedra
entities.body: One of the famous women whose ghost Odysseus sees.

entities.name: Procris
entities.body: One of the famous women whose ghost Odysseus sees.

entities.name: Ariadne
entities.body: Daughter of Minos, carried off from Crete by Theseus and killed by Artemis on Dia.

entities.name: Minos
entities.body: King of Crete at Knossos, who conferred with Zeus every ninth year and now sits in judgement on the dead.

entities.name: Theseus
entities.body: A hero of Athens, one of the great dead Odysseus wished to see.

entities.name: Peirithous
entities.body: Theseus’s companion, host to the Centaur Eurytion among the Lapiths.

entities.name: Eurytion
entities.body: The Centaur whom wine inflamed at Peirithous’s house.

entities.name: Maera
entities.body: One of the women’s ghosts Odysseus names.

entities.name: Clymene
entities.body: One of the women’s ghosts Odysseus names.

entities.name: Eriphyle
entities.body: A ghost Odysseus names, the woman who sold her own husband for gold.

entities.name: Tityus
entities.body: A giant son of Gaia, punished in Hades for assaulting Leto.

entities.name: Tantalus
entities.body: A shade punished in Hades with water and fruit that withdraw whenever he reaches.

entities.name: Sisyphus
entities.body: A shade punished in Hades by rolling a stone that always runs back down.

entities.name: Heracles
entities.body: The greatest of the strong men, whose phantom Odysseus meets in Hades while he himself feasts among the gods. Butler’s original calls him Hercules.

entities.name: The Gorgon
entities.body: The monstrous head Odysseus fears Persephone will send up out of Hades.

entities.name: Rhadamanthus
entities.body: The fair-haired ruler of the Elysian plain.

entities.name: Orion
entities.body: The hunter loved by Dawn and killed by Artemis in Ortygia; he hunts still among the dead.

entities.name: Iasion
entities.body: The man Demeter loved and Zeus struck down.

entities.name: Tithonus
entities.body: Dawn’s consort, from whose side she rises each morning.

entities.name: Cadmus
entities.body: Father of Ino, who became the goddess Leucothea.

entities.name: Erechtheus
entities.body: The king of Athens to whose house Athena goes.

entities.name: Lampus
entities.body: One of the two horses that draw Dawn’s chariot.

entities.name: Phaethon
entities.body: One of the two horses that draw Dawn’s chariot.

entities.name: Actor
entities.body: Father of the maidservant who keeps Penelope’s bedroom door.

entities.name: Melampus
entities.body: The seer and rich man of Pylos, driven out by Neleus, from whom Theoclymenus is descended.

entities.name: Phylacus
entities.body: The king in whose house Melampus was held prisoner for a year.

entities.name: Antiphates
entities.body: A son of Melampus, father of Oicleus.

entities.name: Mantius
entities.body: A son of Melampus, father of Polypheides and Cleitus.

entities.name: Oicleus
entities.body: Son of Antiphates and father of the seer Amphiaraus.

entities.name: Amphiaraus
entities.body: A seer dearly loved by Zeus and Apollo, killed at Thebes through a woman’s bribe.

entities.name: Alcmaeon
entities.body: A son of Amphiaraus.

entities.name: Amphilochus
entities.body: A son of Amphiaraus.

entities.name: Polypheides
entities.body: Son of Mantius and the greatest seer alive after Amphiaraus; Theoclymenus’s father.

entities.name: Cleitus
entities.body: Son of Mantius, carried off by Dawn for his beauty.

entities.name: Castor
entities.body: The rich and honoured Cretan whom Odysseus, in his false story, claims as his father.

entities.name: Hylax
entities.body: Named in Odysseus’s false Cretan story as his supposed grandfather.

entities.name: Aethon
entities.body: The name Odysseus gives Penelope when he tells her he is a Cretan and Idomeneus’s younger brother.

entities.name: Deucalion
entities.body: Named in Odysseus’s false story as Minos’s son and the father of Idomeneus.

entities.name: Eperitus
entities.body: The name Odysseus gives Laertes before telling him the truth.

entities.name: Apheidas
entities.body: A king named in Odysseus’s last false story as his supposed father.

entities.name: Polypemon
entities.body: Named in Odysseus’s last false story as his supposed grandfather.

entities.name: Pheidon
entities.body: King of the Thesprotians, who in Odysseus’s tale entertained him and had news of the real Odysseus.

entities.name: Acastus
entities.body: King of Dulichium, to whom the Thesprotian crew were told to take the beggar.

entities.name: Thoas
entities.body: Son of Andraemon, who in Odysseus’s campfire story ran to the ships and left his cloak behind.

entities.name: Andraemon
entities.body: Father of Thoas.

entities.name: Orsilochus
entities.body: Idomeneus’s son, whom the beggar claims in his story to have killed in Crete.

entities.name: Dmetor
entities.body: A great man of Cyprus, son of Iasus, to whom the beggar says he was given.

entities.name: Iasus
entities.body: Father of Dmetor of Cyprus.

entities.name: Arybas
entities.body: A rich man of Sidon, father of the nurse who carried Eumaeus away.

entities.name: Ctesius
entities.body: Eumaeus’s father, son of Ormenus, king of one of the two communities of Syra.

entities.name: Ormenus
entities.body: Eumaeus’s grandfather.

entities.name: Echetus
entities.body: A king on the mainland held up as a threat, who mutilates everyone brought to him.

entities.name: Iphitus
entities.body: Son of Eurytus, who gave Odysseus the great bow in Messene and was later killed by Heracles.

entities.name: Eurytus
entities.body: The archer of Oechalia who would shoot against the gods; Iphitus’s father.

entities.name: Anchialus
entities.body: Father of Mentes, king of the Taphians.

entities.name: Alcimus
entities.body: Named as Mentor’s father.

entities.name: Alpheus
entities.body: A river spoken of as an ancestor, grandfather of Diocles.

entities.name: The Greeks
entities.body: The army that fought at Troy. The original calls them Achaeans, Argives and Danaans where the modern edition says Greeks.

entities.name: The Trojans
entities.body: The people of Troy, against whom the Greeks fought for nine years.

entities.name: The Phaeacians
entities.body: The seafaring people of Scheria, near kin to the gods, who ferry strangers home.

entities.name: The Cyclopes
entities.body: A lawless people who neither plant nor plough and have no assemblies or laws. The singular Cyclops in this book always means Polyphemus.

entities.name: The Laestrygonians
entities.body: The giant people of Telepylus who wreck Odysseus’s fleet.

entities.name: The Cicons
entities.body: The people of Ismarus, the first Odysseus raided after Troy. The modern edition calls them Cicones.

entities.name: The Thesprotians
entities.body: The mainland people whose king Pheidon figures in the beggar’s story.

entities.name: The Phoenicians
entities.body: Seafaring traders who appear in both the beggar’s tales and Eumaeus’s.

entities.name: The Sidonians
entities.body: The people of Sidon.

entities.name: The Egyptians
entities.body: The people of Egypt, skilled in medicine.

entities.name: The Ethiopians
entities.body: The people at the world’s end, split into two halves, where Poseidon goes to be feasted.

entities.name: The Taphians
entities.body: A seafaring and pirating people; Mentes is their chief.

entities.name: The Myrmidons
entities.body: Achilles’ people, ruled after him by Neoptolemus and by old Peleus.

entities.name: The Cephallenians
entities.body: The people over whom Odysseus and Laertes ruled.

entities.name: The Epeans
entities.body: The people who rule in Elis.

entities.name: The Cretans
entities.body: The people of Crete, among whom the beggar claims his family stood high.

entities.name: The Pylians
entities.body: Nestor’s people.

entities.name: The Lapithae
entities.body: The people among whom the Centaur Eurytion grew violent with wine. The modern edition calls them the Lapiths.

entities.name: The Cimmerians
entities.body: The people who live wrapped in mist and darkness at the edge of Oceanus.

entities.name: The Sintians
entities.body: The people of Lemnos, whose speech Hephaestus calls barbarous.

entities.name: The Solymi
entities.body: A people whose mountains Poseidon passes on his way back from Ethiopia.

entities.name: The Erembians
entities.body: One of the peoples Menelaus visited in his wanderings.

entities.name: The Messenians
entities.body: The people who carried off three hundred Ithacan sheep.

entities.name: The Eteocretans
entities.body: One of the peoples of Crete.

entities.name: The Dorians
entities.body: One of the peoples of Crete, of threefold race.

entities.name: The Pelasgi
entities.body: One of the peoples of Crete. The modern edition calls them the Pelasgians.

entities.name: The Ceteians
entities.body: The people who fell around Eurypylus at Troy. The modern edition calls them the Ceteans.

entities.name: The Cydonians
entities.body: A people of Crete, living around the river Iardanus.

entities.name: The Sicels
entities.body: A people to whom the suitors propose selling the beggar and the seer.

entities.name: The Cauconians
entities.body: A people to whom Athena, as Mentor, says she must go to collect a debt.
